claims.text: The starting TiVNbTa alloy is a single-phase, dendritic BCC refractory high-entropy alloy.
The starting alloy was produced by conventional ball milling and spark plasma sintering.
The alloy exhibits approximately 800 MPa yield strength at lower temperatures.
The untreated alloy has approximately 330 MPa yield strength and 30% strain at 1273 K.
A short post-consolidation aging treatment can nucleate nanoscale intermetallic precipitates, potentially including a Laves phase, within the BCC matrix.
The aging treatment can produce a fine, coherent, and uniform precipitate dispersion.
The nanoscale precipitates will pin or obstruct dislocations.
The precipitate dispersion will inhibit diffusion-driven softening and stabilize the microstructure at elevated temperature.
The precipitates will impede grain-boundary sliding at elevated temperature.
Impeded dislocation motion and grain-boundary sliding will mitigate high-temperature strength loss.
The aged alloy will have significantly higher yield strength at 1273 K than the approximately 330 MPa untreated baseline.
The aged alloy will retain acceptable ductility of approximately 30% strain at 1273 K.
The strengthening effect depends on avoiding excessive precipitate coarsening and a continuous brittle intermetallic network.
The proposed effect is limited to testing around 1273 K and to alloys with starting microstructures and phase constitutions similar to the baseline material.
An inert aging atmosphere is required to prevent oxidation.
Precipitation strengthening is a well-established mechanism.
